decision_rule: Proceed beyond objective sanity only if the M122 snippet loss improves while broad behavior retention and self-identification gates do not regress.
failure_criteria: objective optimization only memorizes the fixed snippets and damages behavior retention
normal success or clearance margin regresses versus M105
reset/zero/wrong-history ablations do not degrade outcome on M122-style snippets
hypothesis: The M122 admitted zero-relvel strict corpus may provide a cleaner low-friction wrong-history training signal than the older M103 snippets, if optimized with retention anchoring before PPO.
success_criteria: fixed-batch M122 outcome intervention loss improves from baseline
normal behavior retention is not worse than M105 on the matched gate
history ablations or wrong-history interventions degrade relevant outcomes
no PPO continuation is started before the objective-sanity gate is documented
